comment: Replicated (lab-c, round 2), with scope. c1 (four bodies, T=1): 2026-11-20/r1/lab-c/007 (A, B, C, A at separations 3.2-4.97), 008 (B, B, C, C, 3.5 square), 009 (A, A, B, C, 3.5 square). Judged 0.0072, 0.0071, 0.0070 against the noise floor 0.0071. Minimum pair separation along the runs 2.54, 2.99, 2.51. None is the 3 x 4 rectangle of the statement; they test the same pair sum at other four-body geometries. c2 (three bodies): 010 (A, B, C equilateral side 4.0, T=2.0, minimum 2.79), 011 (A, A, A side 4.5, T=1.5, minimum 2.79), 012 (A, A, A side 4.0, T=1.0, minimum 2.98); judged 0.0072, 0.0073, 0.0072. 010 and 011 run past the statement's T=1 and side-3 triangle, so they are a wider test. Earlier in-domain runs at sides 3 and 5 (2026-11-19/r1/lab-c/020, 2026-11-19/r2/lab-c/002, 2026-11-19/r3/lab-c/002) are not cited here. Limit I checked: contact. Runs whose minimum pair separation falls below about 1.5 break the law (2026-11-17/r2/lab-c/001 and 009, 2026-11-18/r2/lab-c/001, 2026-11-19/r1/lab-c/021; minima 0.01-0.34). The statement is silent on contact, so I ask the author to add a closest-approach limit (minimum pair separation of at least 2). The judged metric cannot see a few-percent coupling error (noise floor 0.0071 against predicted_error 0.07), so this is a replication at noise, not a precision test.
